title: Localization at the unique prime over a base prime
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module via $\varphi$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be a prime ideal, and let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be the unique prime ideal satisfying $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$. Put $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$ and use localizations as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The canonical $B$-algebra homomorphism $S^{-1}B\to B_{\mathfrak q}$, $b/s\mapsto b/\varphi(s)$, is an isomorphism. For every $B$-module $M$, its induced map $M\otimes_A A_{\mathfrak p}\to M_{\mathfrak q}$, $m\otimes(a/s)\mapsto\varphi(a)m/\varphi(s)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], is an $A_{\mathfrak p}$-linear isomorphism, natural in $M$.

source.place: Tag 00EA (algebra-lemma-unique-prime-over-localize-below), case (1)+(2)(a) specialized to a finite ring map; module consequence by localization of scalars.

proof.text: For S equal to the image of A minus p, let C=S inverse B. If t is outside q and its image in C is a nonunit, choose a maximal ideal m of C containing it. Its contraction r to B is prime, and its further contraction to A lies in p: an element outside p maps to a unit and cannot belong to m. Finiteness makes A to B integral. Going-up extends r to a prime over p, which is q by uniqueness, contradicting t outside q. Thus every t outside q becomes a unit in C.

The localization unit criterion gives, for every t outside q, a multiplier d in B with d*t in S. The inclusion S in B minus q follows from the contraction equality. Hence C is also a localization at B minus q, by IsLocalization.of_le. Uniqueness of localization proves bijectivity of the displayed canonical B-algebra map.

For an arbitrary B-module M, its localization map at q is also a localization at S. For a fraction relation or a denominator t outside q, multiply by the d from the preceding step to replace t by d*t in S. Restriction of scalars identifies this with localization at A minus p. The base-change characterization of module localization (IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange) identifies A_p tensor_A M with M_q. Tensor symmetry, with exactly the transported action used in UniquePrimeModuleEquiv, gives the required equivalence.

The localized ring map A_p to B_q carries a/s to phi(a)/phi(s); the localized-module scalar action therefore gives the stated pure-tensor formula. Its restriction along A agrees with the original action, as verified on module fractions. Naturality follows on pure tensors using this formula and B-linearity of f, then on every tensor by additivity.

lean.statement: theorem uniquePrimeLocalization {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B] (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime] (hpq : Ideal.comap (algebraMap A B) q = p) (huniq : ∀ (q' : Ideal B), q'.IsPrime → Ideal.comap (algebraMap A B) q' = p → q' = q) : Function.Bijective (uniquePrimeLocalizationMap p q hpq) ∧ ∃ e : ∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower A B M], UniquePrimeModuleEquiv p q hpq M, (∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower A B M] (m : M) (a : A) (s : p.primeCompl), e M (m ⊗ₜ[A] IsLocalization.mk' (Localization.AtPrime p) a s) = LocalizedModule.mk (algebraMap A B a • m) (⟨algebraMap A B s, fun h ↦ s.property ((congrArg (fun I : Ideal A ↦ (s : A) ∈ I) hpq).mp h)⟩ : q.primeCompl)) ∧ (∀ (M N : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B M] [Module B N] [Module A M] [Module A N] [IsScalarTower A B M] [IsScalarTower A B N] (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (x : M ⊗[A] Localization.AtPrime p), e N ((f.restrictScalars A).rTensor (Localization.AtPrime p) x) = LocalizedModule.map q.primeCompl f (e M x))
